findings.source_passage: If your bitterest foe were walking straight towards you, with dagger uplifted in broad day, you would not be able to see him
findings.source_locator: paragraph on the whale's sideway vision, after 'thirty more behind it'
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most rhetorically vivid and quotable moments in the chapter—the 'bitterest foe with dagger uplifted' image is signature Ishmael voice, carrying both the comic-dire register and the interpretive point about blindness to frontal threat. Its loss flattens the passage to bare cetological fact.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'bitterest foe...dagger uplifted in broad day' sentence; the surrounding logic can be compressed but this image must appear near-verbatim.

findings.source_passage: you would have two backs, so to speak; but, at the same time, also, two fronts (side fronts): for what is it that makes the front of a man—what, indeed, but his eyes?
findings.source_locator: paragraph on the whale's sideway vision, final sentence
findings.why_it_matters: The rhetorical question 'what is it that makes the front of a man—what, indeed, but his eyes?' is a voice-defining moment of philosophical wit; the draft reduces it to a bare factual summary ('two side fronts and two backs'), entirely erasing the signature phrasing and ironic turn.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve the rhetorical question near-verbatim: 'you would have two backs, so to speak; but also two fronts (side fronts): for what is it that makes the front of a man—what, indeed, but his eyes?'

findings.source_passage: the other will be utterly excluded from your contemporary consciousness. How is it, then, with the whale? True, both his eyes, in themselves, must simultaneously act
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'A curious and most puzzling question'
findings.why_it_matters: The extended philosophical digression on divided consciousness—whether the whale can hold two distinct prospects simultaneously—is compressed to a single subordinate clause. The paragraph's voice-driven epistemological inquiry, including the Euclid analogy context, is largely gone.
findings.suggested_fix: Expand the Euclid analogy passage to preserve at least the phrasing 'as if a man were able simultaneously to go through the demonstrations of two distinct problems in Euclid' as a recognizable fragment, and retain more of the consciousness-splitting argument.

findings.source_passage: this whale is not dead; he is only dispirited; out of sorts, perhaps; hypochondriac; and so supine, that the hinges of his jaw have relaxed, leaving him there in that ungainly sort of plight, a reproach to all his tribe
findings.source_locator: paragraph on the jaw hanging like a jib-boom
findings.why_it_matters: The comic anthropomorphism ('hypochondriac,' 'a reproach to all his tribe, who must imprecate lock-jaws upon him') is entirely absent from the draft. This is signature Melville voice—the comic-digressive narrator reading animal behavior through human social shame.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'only dispirited; out of sorts, perhaps; hypochondriac' and at minimum 'a reproach to all his tribe' to preserve the comic register.

findings.source_passage: the extraordinary vacillations of movement displayed by some whales when beset by three or four boats; the timidity and liability to queer frights...all this indirectly proceeds from the helpless perplexity of volition
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'It may be but an idle whim'
findings.why_it_matters: This paragraph draws the practical-interpretive consequence of the divided-vision argument—whale behavior in the hunt explained by perceptual division. It carries both narrative foreshadowing weight and the chapter's thematic payoff on vision/volition, and is entirely cut.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore at least one sentence linking divided whale vision to 'helpless perplexity of volition' and the erratic behavior of beset whales.

summary: The draft drops two high-severity signature passages (the 'bitterest foe with dagger uplifted' image and the 'what makes the front of a man—but his eyes?' rhetorical climax) and erases three further medium-weight voice and interpretive moments, including the 'hypochondriac' whale comedy and the volition-perplexity paragraph.
